- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to historical mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 30-day horizon when recent sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/–0.20+); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion; if 3–5 consecutive days show price above 1.5σ from historical mean, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until reversion.
- In sentiment-heavy periods (e.g., sentiment >0.50 for 3+ days), model tends to overfit short-term momentum; dampen forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
